title: Derived tensor preserves locally constant finite type cohomology
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B$ a commutative Noetherian ring. If $K,L\in D^-(\mathcal C,\underline B)$ have all cohomology sheaves locally constant of finite type, then every cohomology sheaf of $K\otimes_B^L L$ is locally constant of finite type. Here constants are [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], derived categories and cohomology are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and Noetherian means [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; locally constant of finite type means locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finitely generated module. No existence of points of the site is assumed. Here $D^-$ denotes objects whose cohomology vanishes in sufficiently high degrees, and $K\otimes_B^L L$ denotes the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] after replacing the factors by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex].

proof.text: Use homologyFunctorFactors and the representative isomorphisms to transfer the upper homology bounds and the local constant finite type hypotheses from K,L to P,Q. Local constant finite type is invariant under isomorphism: compose each covering-slice trivialization with the restricted isomorphism.

For fixed i and V, apply local finite-free truncation models to P with cutoff i-bQ and to Q with cutoff i-bP. Intersect the resulting two covering sieves. On an arrow of this intersection obtain E,F, upper term bounds, finite free terms and the two required local derived model isomorphisms.
Apply the local tensor comparison to these supplied models. It identifies H^i of the restricted tensor complex with H^i of the restricted c(T), where T is the algebraic total tensor of E and F.

In degree j, put I={p in Z | j-bF <= p <= bE}. Map the coproduct over I of E^p tensor F^(j-p) to T^j using the total-complex inclusions. This map is epic: test equality of outgoing maps on every total summand; indices outside I have a zero tensor factor by an upper term bound. Every summand is finite, and the coproduct is finite via its finite biproduct/product description. Surjectivity of the epic map in ModuleCat makes T^j finite.
Noetherianity makes cycles, which inject into the finite module T^i, finite. The epimorphism from cycles onto H^i(T) makes that cohomology module finite.

Prove exactness of the actual constant realization used by the statement: evaluation jointly reflects finite limits and finite colimits of constant module presheaves, and module sheafification is exact. ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso therefore identifies H^i(c(T)) with c(H^i(T)). Exact slice restriction likewise commutes with homology by the same short-complex comparison. Compose these two restriction comparisons, the constant-realization comparison and the tensor comparison. The intersection cover and the finite module H^i(T) are precisely the witnesses in the definition of local constant finite type.

tool_uses.why: Local representatives and equality justify the sheaf tensor comparison under restriction to a slice; the unit has no general sheafification tool of its own.
Use the already defined general ringed-site derived tensor on K-flat flat representatives, rather than any etale-only tensor construction.
Apply the existing arbitrary-ringed-site flat restriction theorem to the chosen bounded-above flat representatives.
Use exact constant realization on an arbitrary small site, including its preservation of quasi-isomorphisms; this is general coefficient infrastructure.
Use finite generation of cycles in finite modules over B; this commutative-algebra tool is already a Mathlib leaf.
Use exact restriction for module sheaves to commute with cohomology; no etale or enough-points hypothesis is required.
Use bounded-above flat replacements with the given upper term bounds on a general ringed site.
Use K-flatness of bounded-above flat complexes both before and after restriction and for constant free models.
